title: WPMS/84/2013 of SWAMI KESHWACHARYA CHELA SWAMI RANGACHARYA Vs LORD LAXMINARAYAN JI MAHARAJ

paras.text:
WPMS No. 84 of 2013
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
(Via Video Conferencing)
Mr. Arvind Kumar Sharma, Advocate for
the petitioner.
Mr. B. M. Pingal, Advocate for the
respondent.
The petitioner had filed this Writ Petition
challenging the impugned order dated 01.12.2012,
as was passed by the Court of 4
th Additional
District Judge, Haridwar in Civil Appeal No.24 of
1998, Swami Rangacharya Vs. Laxmi Narayan
and others, as well as the order dated 03.02.2003,
which was passed by the same Judge in the same
proceedings, by virtue of which the petitioners
application preferred under Order 22 Rule 3, 4
and 9 to be read with Section 151 of the CPC, has
been rejected, on the ground of being barred by
the limitation. The limitation for the purposes of
considering the substitution may not be construed
in a technical manner, as it hampers the very
purpose of an effective adjudication of the
proceedings on its own merit. The technicalities in
filing the substitution application on account of
bar of limitation runs contrary to the interest of
adjudicating the lis on its own merit.
Apart from it, as against the impugned
orders of rejecting the application of the
petitioner, being paper no.74 d by the impugned
judgment dated 01.12.2012, the respondent had
put in appearance in the Writ Petition; as a
caveator and they were heard as a caveator at the
time when the Writ Petition was entertained and
the counter affidavit was called upon by an order
dated 11.01.2013. The notices have been issued to
the respondent and no counter affidavit has been
filed by any of the respondent, till date, including
the caveator.
Owing to the aforesaid circumstances and
considering the fact that bringing the heirs on
record of the deceased party to the proceedings of

the Appeal, would rather be in the interest of
justice, consequently, this Writ Petition is
allowed, the impugned order is quashed, the
Learned 4th Additional District Judge, Haridwar,
is hereby directed to decide the application paper
no. 74 d and the substitution application
accompanying with it exclusively on its own merit
rather than dismissing the same on the ground of
limitation.
However, the said direction which has been
issued for considering the application under Order
22 Rule 2, 3, 4 and 9 would be subject to the
condition that the proceeding before the court
below has not already been decided, as on date.
